questions.q: A couple wants a temporary method that also lowers the risk of sexually transmitted infections. Which choice best satisfies both goals according to the Exemplar?
options: A) Condoms, because they act as barriers to insemination and also reduce STD risk
B) Vasectomy, because it is easily reversible and prevents all STDs
C) MTP, because it is a routine contraceptive method after every coitus
D) ZIFT, because it blocks sperm entry into the cervix
questions.answer: A) Condoms, because they act as barriers to insemination and also reduce STD risk
questions.explanation: The Exemplar lists condoms as effective barriers for insemination and also states that they help reduce the risk of sexually transmitted diseases. Vasectomy is a surgical sterilisation method and is treated as almost irreversible, while MTP is not a routine contraceptive method. ZIFT is an assisted reproductive technique, not a barrier contraceptive.

questions.q: A mother is intensely lactating and temporarily does not conceive. Which endocrine explanation and contraceptive principle are most consistent with this condition?
options: A) Hypersecretion of gonadotropins causes repeated ovulation
B) Suppression of gonadotropins can produce lactational amenorrhoea and reduce the chance of ovulation
C) Suppression of fertilisation occurs because the fallopian tubes are surgically blocked
D) Increased gamete transport prevents implantation
questions.answer: B) Suppression of gonadotropins can produce lactational amenorrhoea and reduce the chance of ovulation
questions.explanation: The Exemplar directly associates intense lactation with suppression of gonadotropins. Reduced gonadotropin activity can suppress ovulation and produce lactational amenorrhoea. This is why lactational amenorrhoea can function as a natural contraceptive method for a limited period.

questions.q: A copper-releasing IUD is compared with a non-medicated IUD. Which explanation best accounts for the higher contraceptive efficiency of the copper-releasing device?
options: A) It permanently destroys the ovaries
B) It suppresses all gametogenesis in both partners
C) It combines the uterine foreign-body response, including increased phagocytosis, with an additional copper-mediated reduction in sperm effectiveness
D) It is inserted into the uterus by the user without medical assistance
questions.answer: C) It combines the uterine foreign-body response, including increased phagocytosis, with an additional copper-mediated reduction in sperm effectiveness
questions.explanation: The Exemplar states that IUDs increase phagocytosis in the uterus and separately asks why copper-releasing IUDs are more efficient than non-medicated devices. The higher efficiency follows because copper adds a sperm-inhibitory effect to the basic uterine response. The other choices contradict the source because IUDs do not destroy ovaries, suppress all gametogenesis, or require self-insertion.

questions.q: Which assisted reproductive procedure is correctly identified for directly injecting a sperm into an ovum?
questions.explanation: The Exemplar explicitly identifies intracytoplasmic sperm injection as the technique in which a sperm is directly injected into an ovum. GIFT involves transfer of gametes to the fallopian tube, while ZIFT involves transfer of a zygote. ET is a broader embryo-transfer procedure, so ICSI is the precise answer.
